lead: the two lights in you sit at the greatest distance this road allows. what other people have lost comes up through you intact, and what is in you was put there by people who no longer remember putting it.
sun: the faculty works, and it works at distance. somebody comes to you about a thing they wrote off years ago, a friendship or a trade or a version of themselves from before a bad decade, and you go down for it and it comes up in one piece. all of it points outward, and there has never been anything at your own end for it to take hold of.
moon: underneath, things do not go missing, because nothing was ever seen to arrive. the room takes what people set down in it and files no date, no owner, no record of a before. so retrieval has no purchase there. bringing a thing up requires having watched it go down, and every item in you was already in place by the time you looked.
pull: the reach and the store are at opposite ends of you, the full width of the road between them, and everything you have ever recovered was somebody else's.
tension: someone who loves you spent four months finding a person you had lost touch with, and watched it land nowhere. the delight was real and the wrong size, and she saw that too. what came of it was you never let anybody do anything for you, said without heat. she has the shape of it right and the cause wrong: nothing in you had been short of him.
cost: what everybody agreed was gone comes back up through you in usable condition, on no notice, for people who had already done their grieving over it, and they remember it for the rest of their lives. run the other way and the same reach closes on air. what is in you got in without a departure attached, so there is nothing down there with a way up.

lead: he told you one thing in a bad winter and has not referred to it since, and would say it was dealt with. you hear it under every sentence he has said to you in the eleven years after.
sun: a thing told once is supposed to have a life: given, held, and put down by both parties at about the same time. yours never reaches the last part. the winter is not over in you, so you go back into it — a question at the right moment, a reference nobody else at that table could make — and the material is exactly as current as the night it was handed over.
moon: what goes in here is the pressure under a sentence, and pressure has no expiry on it. words age, a state does not. so you are holding him at his worst hour, live, in the form it had before he tidied it, and he never knew any of it left him, which is why he has never once tried to get it back.
pull: everybody you love has been allowed to become somebody else. no part of that reached the version of them you are keeping, which is the only one left in the room where it started.
tension: you asked after it once, at the right moment, and the room did not hear the question but he did. what he heard was that a night he has spent eleven years getting out from under is a live item somewhere outside himself. nothing you said was wrong. good memory gets said afterwards, in a tone that is not warm, and there is no correcting it — telling him you kept it because it never closed makes the keeping deliberate.
cost: years on, a person finds that what they handed over in a bad fortnight was carried the whole time with no condition attached, and that is rare enough to change what they think is available from anybody. the keeping runs past the trouble it was for. everybody near you is kept at the temperature of their hardest hour by someone they stopped confiding in long ago.

lead: the racket in any room you are in is largely yours, and it is what everybody else sets their watch by. you have never once heard a silence as a decision somebody made.
sun: a stop, in you, is a gap. the sunday thing that fell away, the band, the standing table — none of it registers as over, so you start it again, at the tempo it was running at before, which is the only tempo you have for it. nobody has to be persuaded, because a beat is not an argument, and refusing one in public is not a thing people can do.
moon: the beat does not carry through a silence the way you do. it exists only while somebody is putting it out, so a quiet week is not neutral — the room reads a stopped sound the only way one can be read, and starts arranging itself around whatever has gone wrong. from where you are nothing has stopped. you are between passes, which has no sound to it.
pull: you can start anything again, at the old tempo, and everyone will come. the one sound you cannot make is a deliberate silence — every quiet you have kept was heard as a fault.
tension: they had let it go last autumn, on purpose, without anybody saying so — that is how a group ends something it cannot vote on. you read the quiet as a lapse and sent the message, and everyone came, because nobody can say out loud that they were glad it had stopped. it runs again, and four of the six at that table are attending a thing they meant to be over, and each believes the others want it.
cost: two families that were not yours are speaking again because you walked in and made noise at them until the thing had a beat, which is not a service anybody advertises. the equipment does not idle. a bad season of your own arrives as a system fault, so it gets answered with concern and never with quiet, which is the one thing it needed.

lead: there is a bed made up in your house for a man who has not been in the country for six years, and he knows it, and knowing it is the heaviest thing anybody has ever given him.
sun: the room is not a gesture. you make it because he is coming back, which you have never had cause to doubt, and the making is ordinary work on a schedule nobody sees: the sheets, the shelf left as he had it, the chair that does not get given away when the house needs a chair. what you are doing is preparing for an event.
moon: space made for a person is not neutral toward them. an open door can be walked past; a room with his name on it cannot. you put no term on it and did not have to — what gets held in a space here binds whoever it was held for. he has worked out that the house expects a return from him, and he never agreed to one.
pull: you have kept a place for everybody who left, and a place kept is not a thing anyone can hand back. the ones who understood that are the ones who stopped coming.
tension: a person can turn down an invitation. nobody has a way to turn down a room, so the ones who wanted to be done with this house have gone on arriving at it, warmly, for years, without being able to locate what is wrong. you have asked nobody for anything and everybody can feel a request in it. saying so would mean telling you the welcome was a hold, and the evidence is a made bed.
cost: somebody can arrive at two in the morning in whatever condition they are in and find the place ready, with no questions at the door and nothing to be explained in the week after. what goes into the room does not come out unattached. the two who never came back are the ones who read it correctly, and neither has been able to say so.
